title: serving runtime weekly update - kernel, KV cache, batching (2026-07-29)
body:
Summary:
- This week focused on three parallel tracks: attention/kernel micro-optimizations, KV cache correctness and eviction tuning, and the adaptive batching scheduler. Goal was to stabilize recent perf wins and get a canary rollout for the kernel refactor by EOW.

Kernel work (owner: Aisha):
- Merged PR #842 (attention-kernel-refactor): reworked inner-loop to reduce register pressure and improved vectorization across multi-head attention.
- Results: on H100 p4d-like instances we see 8-12% median token latency reduction for small sequence (<=512) and up to 18% throughput improvement for batched generation workloads. Tail (95th) latency improved ~6%.
- Known issues: an edge-case in rotary embedding handling caused incorrect outputs for a specific positional-offset pattern; patched in hotfix PR #856. Unit tests added.
- Next: run cross-hardware regression matrix (A100/H100/RTX6000) and produce table of kernel perf deltas for release notes.

KV cache (owner: Ravi):
- Deployed eviction-policy changes to canary (10% traffic). New policy: LRU with prefix-awareness (prioritizes keeping recently used prefixes across sessions).
- Observed metrics on canary (chat workload): cache hit rate moved from 28% -> 46% after policy change and after increasing default per-session cache budget by 1.5x. This reduced average upstream compute per request by ~12% and token cost down ~9% for canary users.
- Fixed a bug where stale entries were not invalidated on model variant switch (SRV-4321). Root cause: metadata key collision when model flavor suffix was missing. Patch deployed and validated.
- Remaining risk: memory amplification under long-lived sessions with adversarial token streams. Mitigation: scheduled background compaction job and per-session hard cap enforcement (SRV-4350).
- Next: expand canary to 30% next Tuesday pending stability; prepare runbook for rollback and outage detection (alerts already added to console).

Batching (owner: Monica):
- Adaptive batching scheduler experiment 3 rolled out in staging. Scheduler now considers three signals: request age, current queue size, and recent model latency trend to decide dynamic batch cutpoints.
- Results: for mid-size seq workloads (avg seq 1024) throughput improved ~15% with median latency kept within SLO (+3ms). Tail latency remained stable.
- Observed a corner case: when request arrival rate oscillates rapidly (bursty chat), scheduler oscillates between small and very large batches causing jitter. Workaround: added short hysteresis window (200ms) which reduced oscillation but increased median latency by ~1.2ms.
- Next: tune hysteresis and add test harness to simulate bursty arrival patterns at scale; run e2e A/B against current scheduler for one-week window.

Standup highlights / blockers:
- Blocker: one open memory leak in quantized path when using KV cache + batching on very long context (>40k tokens). Repro steps and heap traces captured; investigating root cause (likely interaction between kv shard cleanup and quantized buffer reuse). Assigned to Ravi and Andrew.
- Blocker: docs for kernel ABI changes still not merged — will block downstream infra teams. Aisha to finish docs draft by Friday.

Operational notes / metrics:
- Canary health: 10% traffic on kernel refactor and KV policy. No customer-facing errors observed; internal error rate stable.
- Perf numbers (canary vs baseline): median token latency -10%; throughput +15% (batched gen); cache hit rate +18pp for chat workload.
- Cost estimate: if canary results hold, projected inference spend reduction of ~7-9% for serviced customers using caching + batching improvements.

Decisions made:
- Ramp kernel refactor canary from 10% -> 30% next Tue if no regressions in perf and correctness tests.
- Expand KV canary to 30% and enable background compaction job one week after ramp.
- Hold full rollout of adaptive batching until hysteresis tuning and A/B run complete.

Action items / owners:
- Aisha: finalize kernel ABI docs, run cross-hardware perf matrix, open release note draft (ETA Mon).
- Ravi: spike to reproduce long-context mem leak, add compaction telemetry, coordinate canary ramp (ETA Wed).
- Monica: add bursty-workload harness, tune scheduler hysteresis, prepare A/B test config (ETA next Fri).
- Andrew: help on quantized buffer debug and run heavy repros (ETA Thu).
- SRE: add extra alerting for cache eviction rates and batch size oscillation (created ticket: SRV-4392).

Notes / links:
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842, https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/856
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRV/KV+Cache+Design
- Jira tickets: SRV-4321 (kv variant invalidation), SRV-4350 (compaction/hard-caps), SRV-4392 (alerts)

Quick wins for next week:
- Merge kernel docs + perf table
- Ramp canaries to 30% if green
- Add compaction telemetry and start long-context mem leak RCA

If anything needs immediate attention ping #eng-serving-runtime or add to the weekly sync agenda.

— Liam
